newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi to boost share of GDI-engined cars.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi to boost share of GDI-engined cars.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Tuesday it aims to boost the share of gasoline direct injection-engined (GDI) cars as a portion of total domestic sales of gasoline-engined cars to 80 percent from 50 percent by 1999.
In GDI-engined cars, fuel is injected directly into cylinders to achieve an ultra-lean burn effect, while fuel is injected through the intake-manifold in conventional lean-burn engines.
Mitsubishi earlier said GDI would reduce fuel consumption by 35 percent compared with its predecessor, cut emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) by 35 percent and increase engine power by 10 percent.

Mitsubishi also said on Tuesday it had launched a partially remodelled Diamante, its flagship luxury sedan, equipped with a 3-litre GDI engine. The car is also equipped with a navigation system, and front seat and side airbags. It hopes to sell 3,000 Diamantes a month.

Mitsubishi installed a 3.5-litre GDI engine in its popular Pajero heavy sport-utility vehicle in May. It introduced a 1.8-litre GDI engine last August in its new Galant medium luxury sedan and Legnum station wagon models.
Mitsubishi's Kyoto plant will boost output of GDI engines to 30,000 units per month by end-1997 and to more than 40,000 in 1998 from the present 20,000, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Mitsubishi said last Friday it would invest about 23 billion yen to build a new plant in Yagi, Kyoto prefecture, western Japan, to produce continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) systems.
Mitsubishi did not disclose details of its CVT system, which it said can reduce fuel consumption.
The plant will start output of CVTs in 1999 with a monthly capacity of 24,000 units.

In September 1995, Honda Motor Co Ltd launched a 1.5-litre Civic with a CVT transmission system and new engine, reducing fuel consumption by 20 percent and increasing engine power output by 40 percent.
The CVT system is usually used in small cars such as Nissan Motor Co Ltd's March model (called Micra abroad), Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd's 660cc Vivio car and Domingo van and Fiat SpA's Panda model.
